name: Reservoir rUSD
oneLiner: rUSD is Reservoir's mintable dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC, USDT, or USD1 and backed by a mixed RWA and digital-asset balance sheet.
collateral: Reservoir protocol balance sheet of stablecoin PSM liquidity, RWA allocations, DeFi lending markets, and governance-approved credit strategies monitored through Reservoir's live reserve endpoint
pegMechanism: Users can mint and redeem rUSD 1:1 against USDC, USDT, or USD1 through Reservoir's Peg Stability Module, while Credit Enforcer contracts constrain liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before protocol asset reallocations.

applicabilityBasis.summary: rUSD is a USD-pegged, 1:1 mintable/redeemable stablecoin that structurally meets the GENIUS Act definition of a payment stablecoin. However, the issuer explicitly excludes US persons from the protocol and interface via its Terms of Service, and the ToS is governed by Cayman Islands law, indicating the issuer has not sought any US regulatory pathway.

genius.notes: The Reservoir Terms of Service explicitly state that rUSD is not offered to US persons and that US persons are not permitted to use the Interface or Protocol. The ToS is governed by Cayman Islands law. No named legal issuer entity is disclosed; the protocol is operated by Reservoir Protocol, incubated by Fortunafi. No GENIUS Act pathway, PPSI application, or foreign exception engagement was identified.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: Reservoir's ToS explicitly bars US persons from rUSD; Cayman Islands governing law and absence of any named US legal entity confirm the issuer has not engaged with GENIUS Act compliance. No PPSI approval, state-qualified approval, official application, or foreign exception registration was found.

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from Reservoir's stablecoin collateral and PSM exposure to tracked freezable stablecoins such as USDC, USDT, USD1, PYUSD, RLUSD, GHO, and AUSD.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: rUSD inherits upstream freeze risk because the Reservoir balance sheet and PSM are built around tracked stablecoins with issuer or governance control surfaces.

mintAuthority.summary: rUSD issuance runs through Reservoir PSMs and the Credit Enforcer. Both the PSM and Credit Enforcer share the same DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder: Reservoir EOA 0xb7570e32.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Reservoir rUSD is deployed across many chains and issuer docs list official contract addresses. No external bridge protocol was resolved, so reviewed evidence supports issuer/protocol-native multichain minting rather than a liquidity bridge.

sources.label: Sentora PRIME vault launch note (curator-primary: PRIME is Figure-originated HELOC credit)

reserveReview.rationale: The Reservoir raw reserves API fetched on 2026-07-20 reported $36,081,690.31 of total assets across 11 rows (totalLiabilities $35,792,938.51, equity $288,751.80). Bucketing rows through the reviewed Reservoir adapter mapping yields: Hastra/Sentora PRIME 44.8% ($120,025.13 Hastra PRIME token + $16,049,634.78 Morpho Sentora PRIME), Pendle PT-USDat-27AUG2026 25.3% ($9,124,818.98), Aave GHO on Plasma/Monad 15.3% ($5,520,885.92), USDC 9.9% ($201,441.69 direct/PSM USDC + $3,367,032.94 Morpho Steakhouse Prime Instant V2), USD1 2.1% ($251,532.71 direct + $496,413.08 Morpho Steakhouse High Yield USD1 on Monad), and the unmapped Agua Global Carry Vault 2.6% ($949,905.09); rounded slices sum to 100.0%. Since the 2026-07-14 review the USD1 bucket fell from 8.4% to 2.1% (a 6.3-point move outside the +/-5-point binding band), so curated weights were re-aligned to the 2026-07-20 live rows; the other five buckets moved less than 2 points. Risk-tier judgment calls: PRIME stays high because it is Figure-originated HELOC private credit (per curator Sentora's own description) whose exit path is an unpublished Morpho market redemption; PT USDat stays high despite tokenized-treasury collateral because the position is a fixed-maturity Pendle principal token (matures 2026-08-27, 38 days out) carrying AMM-exit basis risk, so the riskier tier was kept over low tokenized-Treasury treatment; the Agua ERC-4626 multi-strategy vault remains unmapped because Reservoir discloses no constituent breakdown.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Reservoir raw reserves API (app.reservoir.xyz/api/reserves/raw) fetched 2026-07-20; totalBalanceValue rows bucketed through the reviewed Reservoir live-reserve adapter mapping and normalized against totalAssets $36,081,690.31
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The 2.6% Agua Global Carry Vault row (multi-strategy ERC-4626 across lending markets, protocols, and chains) does not expose a constituent-level allocation that supports a tracked-stablecoin mapping.

providers.name: Reservoir Protocol on-chain Asset Adapter / PSM contracts (self-custodied balance sheet; no third-party custodian)

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-3 (lead usdd-tron-dao-reserve)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Reservoir's balance sheet sits in protocol-controlled Asset Adapter and PSM contracts (the 2026-07-20 API rows resolve to adapter addresses 0x4809010926aec940b550d34a46a52739f996d75d, 0x3063C5907FAa10c01B242181Aa689bEb23D2BD65, 0x289C204B35859bFb924B9C0759A4FE80f610671c, and 0x8Cc5a546408C6cE3C9eeB99788F9EC3b8FA6b9F3), and neither the Terms of Service (2024-08-23) nor any docs.reservoir.xyz page reviewed today names a third-party custodian, trust, SPV, or holder claim on reserve assets, so no bankruptcy-remoteness structure is documented. Reserve re-use is the protocol's core yield model: docs state the balance sheet is allocated into RWA, lending markets, and DeFi strategies, and the ToS itself warns redemptions can lag when reserve assets must be sold or redeemed. Protocol admins (the PSM and Credit Enforcer DEFAULT_ADMIN is EOA 0xb7570e32 per the mint-authority review) can reallocate the balance sheet without holder consent. For the 44.8% PRIME sleeve, custody of the underlying Figure HELOC collateral sits upstream with Hastra/Democratized Prime and is not documented by Reservoir. No named legal issuer entity is disclosed (Cayman Islands governing law only), so holder recourse in an insolvency is untested; wallet-level segregation inside the adapter contracts is not disclosed.
